About this citation

Several letters quote an earlier author — Cleanthes, Hecato, Epicurus — and in those the quoted sentence is that author's, delivered in Seneca's Latin. The archive records the inner attribution in the source field where it is known.

Reading the cited source

The archive attributes this English wording to Letters to Lucilius, Ep. 1.1–3 and files it under Stoicism.

What a locator tells you, and what it does not · How this archive traces a quotation

About Seneca

Lucius Annaeus Seneca (c. 4 BCE–65 CE) was a Cordoban-born Stoic, tragic playwright, and adviser—later forced suicide victim—under Nero.

How to read this passage

Is time a river, a dimension, or a structure of consciousness? Augustine, Bergson, and modern metaphysics offer rival pictures while ethics asks how finite time should be spent. This passage enters that discussion through time, attention, autonomy.

What is the source of the quotation “All else belongs to others; time alone is…”?

“All else belongs to others; time alone is…” comes from Letters to Lucilius, Ep. 1.1–3 (c. 62–65 CE), attributed to Seneca.

What does Seneca mean by time?

Is time a river, a dimension, or a structure of consciousness? Augustine, Bergson, and modern metaphysics offer rival pictures while ethics asks how finite time should be spent. This passage enters that discussion through time, attention, autonomy.
